author: blu
body: The port is the plug's, not this script's. The guest dials its own port in net-session-new and the NAT maps that straight through, so listening on anything else hangs the run with no diagnostic. Derived from the plug path rather than passed, so a caller cannot get it wrong by omission.

target: section:S05 -- Send input as ONE FRAMED MESSAGE
author: blu
body: The plugs speak the framed protocol from codex/os/net: net-io-recv-loop waits for a length-prefixed message and answers with one. A raw send leaves the plug waiting, and it eventually prints FAIL having emitted nothing, which reads exactly like a plug that crashed. Do NOT half-close either: the plug replies on this same connection and closes it itself.

target: section:S07 -- Check output, unframe the reply, write
author: blu
body: THE REPLY IS NOT FRAMED, THOUGH THE REQUEST MUST BE. The plugs read with net-io-recv-loop, which requires a length prefix, and answer with net-io-send-text, which does not add one. Stripping five bytes unconditionally therefore eats the first five characters of the emitted source, which still greps and still looks plausible line by line. Only strip a header that is actually there, and prove it is there by its own length field.
